sentences.text: Wpcrl/430/2023 on 22 March, 2023

Author: Ravindra Maithani
Bench: Ravindra Maithani
Wpcrl No.430 of 2023
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Mr. Jai Anant Dehadrai, Mr. Sidharth Arora and Mr. Vipul Sharma, Advocates for the petitioners.
Ms. Manisha Rana Singh, A.G.A. with Ms. Shivali Joshi, Brief Holder for the State.
Mr. Sudhir Kumar, Advocate for Caveator.

The petitioners seek quashing of FIR No.0035 of 2023, dated 31.01.2023, under Sections 420, 406,
120-B, 323, 504 and 506 IPC, Police Station Ranipur, District Haridwar.
Heard.
The FIR in the instant case has been lodged by the respondent no.4, the informant.

According to it,
the informant had been supplying some raw materials to the petitioners.
The informant continued supplying raw materials, but the payments were, most of the time, delayed.
The FIR has little details, but in nut shell, it states that more than Rs. 38 crores were due on the petitioners, which the petitioners have taken dishonestly and fraudulently .

Learned counsel for the petitioners would submit that the petitioners are clean hands before the Court; they are facing insolvency proceedings; their accounts have already been freezed; they admit that there are some dues towards the informant.

Learned counsel for the informant, who is present on the caveat, would submit that despite the accounts of the petitioners being declared non-performing assets, they continued purchasing raw materials from the informant.
It, according to learned counsel for the informant, shows the dishonest intention of the petitioners.
The question, that would fall for determination in this petition is as to whether the dispute is purely civil in nature, without any element or criminality?
Or, have the petitioners dishonest intentions since inception when they entered in their business dealings with the informant?
Having considered, this Court is of the view that this matter requires deliberations.
List this matter on 23.06.2023.
State as well as the informant may file objections.

Till the date fixed, no coercive steps shall be taken against the petitioners, provided they cooperate with the investigation.

When these lines were dictated, learned counsel for the informant would submit that the informant apprehends that the petitioners may leave the country and would delay the investigation and also would avoid payments to many other creditors.

At this stage, on behalf of the petitioners, it is stated that one of the petitioners, i.e. petitioner no.3,
is physically challenged.
He has to visit abroad for his treatment.
Having considered these circumstances, which have been revealed, let the petitioners deposit their passports in the court of Chief Judicial mMagistrate, Haridwar within a week from today.
For this purpose, the petitioners need not remain personally present before the court concerned.

In case, the petitioners, or any of them has to visit abroad for any reason, whatsoever, they can move an application before the court concerned, which shall be considered keeping in view the circumstances explained in such application.
(Ravindra Maithani J.) 22.03.2023 RV WPCRL/430/2023 on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133701716/
